newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH C.BANKER SEES ZLOTY RISE AFTER RATE RISE.
newsitem.headline: POLISH C.BANKER SEES ZLOTY RISE AFTER RATE RISE.

text.p: The zloty, recently weakened by floods and uninspiring current account data, is likely to get a boost from the central bank's interest rate rise on August 4, the president of the National Bank of Poland said on Friday.
"I would expect the zloty to get a boost, maybe not much, but nevertheless a boost from the interest rate rise, because this is standard market behaviour," Hanna Gronkiewicz-Waltz said.

The zloty has now stabilised at around -1.0 to -1.5 percent from the parity rate after concern over the future of Poland's current account prompted a zloty selling spree in July and took it down to all-time lows at -5.5 percent from parity.
The currency trades within a 14 percent band centered around the parity rate.

Markets were also concerned about additional government spending on the reconstruction of areas hit by floods, the worst in centuries, which would increase domestic demand and imports, widening the already high trade gap.
The central bank has stepped in with several symbolic zloty buying interventions to aid the currency.
